_comment: Example profile showing every option. Copy to ~/.config/asbx/profiles/ and edit - real hosts and secret paths belong there, not in version control. `asbx profile show NAME` prints what a profile resolves to.
_comment_env: Non-secret values delivered to the guest as environment variables, alongside the capability placeholders. Base URLs and usernames go here; credentials never do.
_comment_aws_autosign: Opts the session into re-signing every AWS request the guest makes, for any AWS host the session's destination policy already allows - not one declared here. box start mints a random dummy AWS key for the guest (it never holds a real one); signing_secret is the real credential the broker signs with, read fresh on every request rather than cached, since it often carries its own short expiration (an STS session from `aws configure export-credentials`, say) outside asbx's control. See README's 'AWS requests' section.

capabilities._comment_deny: deny_paths is checked before paths, so a broad allow can keep a few endpoints out of reach. Use it where an API mixes routine and destructive operations under one prefix.
capabilities._comment_ttl: ttl is in seconds, and 0 - the default - means the capability never expires, because an agent may run for days. Set it only for a grant meant to lapse on its own; extend one with `asbx cap renew`.
